- PARP1 interacts with MRE11 through specific residues, often involving electrostatic interactions (basic/positively charged residues interacting with acidic/negatively charged residues on the partner protein)
- K548R: Lysine → Arginine (both positively charged, conservative change)
- R548K: Arginine → Lysine (both positively charged, conservative change)
- K547R: Lysine → Arginine at a different position (conservative change)
- K548D: Lysine → Aspartic acid (charge reversal from +1 to -1, non-conservative)

A charge-reversal mutation (K548D) would be the most disruptive to an electrostatic protein-protein interaction, as it not only changes the side chain structure but completely reverses the charge at that position. This would most effectively impair the interaction between PARP1 and MRE11 in co-immunoprecipitation assays.
